items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: I think one day I was at the market with Bob Coquille, do you remember that?

ctx.x: Yeah, that's right. We had a good little band at the original 25 Club. That was back off the Pontchartrain Road where the Honeysuckle Inn was. You may have heard of the Honeysuckle Inn. The Honeysuckle Inn and the original 25 Club were right across from each other. Is that? Sharky opened at the original 25 Club and then left there and went across the street to the Honeysuckle Inn. And I was playing over at the original 25 Club with Eddie Miller and Bill Padron. And I think Sharky was playing over at the other, at…
There's a place, I think one day I was at the market with Bob Coquille, do you remember that? It was about the original 2 Bits Club, is that the same thing?

The original 2 Bits Club, that's it. That's right. That's what, everything was 25 cents. Did they sell whiskey? No, that was in prohibition days. They couldn't sell whiskey. That's why they charged 25 cents. A bowl of ice was 25, a Coca-Cola was 25. The sandwich was 25 cents. Anything you ordered was 25 cents. And of course if you brought your own bottle of whiskey in, you paid 25 cents for the privilege of bringing in your own whiskey. And they did pretty good business too, even at that.
